name: WLW Saturday Night Superstars (1996), Part 1

date.source: Undated in the source; the 1996 broadcast survives only as the relaunch operator's own 30 March 1997 repost, and no month or day is given in either post. Cited for identity only, per this wing's own tier scope -- the 1996 corpus is not otherwise accessioned.

matches.note: Tidalwave's manager, Poseidon, slips him a loaded object at ringside for the finish.

notes: Reposted by the fed's own founding operator on 30 March 1997 during the first relaunch attempt, explicitly to reassert continuity with the original 1995-96 federation -- the surviving record's only card-class document. This is the whole of the 1996 corpus this pass accessions; the rest of the original run (a further three weekly episodes, a sixteen-part pay-per-view, an awards ceremony) is cited in this wing's own provenance notes for identity only and not separately mined or served.

name: WLW Night of the Hunted, Part 1

date.source: Posted to the newsgroup 13 Apr 1996, subject “WLW ‘NIGHT OF THE HUNTED’ PART 1” (msg_id mNjfirAK27MJ), announced live on-air (“5 seconds till world feed”).

matches.note: This collection's surviving Part 1 text breaks off mid-match (Raekwon has just rammed Hayes' head into the ring apron); no result survives in this collection's holdings. Raekwon managed by Slick Rick; Hayes managed by Corley Ripburger (neither separately minted).

notes: WLW President Randy Ventura opens the show and introduces a real-world musical guest, Maverick recording artist Alanis Morissette, performing the anthem -- a public figure's own cameo, not a wrestling persona, not separately minted. Commentary previews the full advertised card: a main event billed as “the entire world is talking about” between Gigantor and Samhain; a four-team scaffold match for the tag team titles (teams not named in the surviving text); and the crowning of the first-ever WLW North American Champion, Rick Styles against Banger. None of these three matches is in the held record's surviving Part 1 text -- flagged as a lead for a future pass if a later part of this series is ever recovered. Ring announcer Bernie Crumb, not separately minted.

name: WLW Achievement Awards, Part 1

date.source: Posted to the newsgroup 28 Apr 1996, subject “WLW ACHIEVEMENT AWARDS! PART 1” (msg_id PmBSZjkWML0J).

notes: The WLW's own first in-house awards special, hosted from the WLW Tower in downtown Toronto by all three of the wing's own broadcast team (Mike Baldwin, Johnny Townsand and Tom Russel), voted on by the fed's own participants. The held record's surviving Part 1 text covers five of what a full ceremony implies were more categories, ending at a commercial break; a later part, if one survives, is a lead for a future pass. This document carries 1 redaction: a real name, spoken by the broadcast team as an unrelated aside, removed per the privacy rule.
